newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower on sharp money rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower on sharp money rate falls.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday amid active short-covering on U.S. dollars triggered by falling short-term interest rates, dealers said.
The local unit closed at T$27.863 against Wednesday's T$27.846 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$229 million.

Taiwan's overnight interbank rate, which spiked into double digits between June 26 and July 1, tumbled to 6.035 percent in late-day trade from Wednesday's 9.813 close. The 30-day commercial paper had fallen to 6.00-6.50 from 7.50-8.00.
"The sudden sharp rate falls prompted many banks to rush to cover their short positions on U.S. dollars," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
She said the local currency was dampened further by the greenback's general buoyancy overseas.
"There is more room for the Taiwan dollar to fall if the U.S. dollar continues to be strong overseas," said another dealer.
A T$27.85-90 range was seen for Friday.
